review.verdict: The headline-and-labels carry the joke, but the two key props that should carry the visual punchline — the empty chair and the glasses — are effectively invisible due to overlap and clipping, and the composition is bottom-heavy with a very similar layout to recent blueprint pieces; this doesn't clear the bar today.
revisionNotes: The empty chair (the brief's stated punchline) is invisible — it's attached to the building's right side at the same spot as the chart component and gets hidden behind it. Reposition chart further right (x~0.46) so the chair reads clearly sliding out the door.

The glasses clip outside the safe area (x 904–1034, per lint) and show only as a stray white rectangle near the human's shoulder instead of sitting on a face. Scale glasses to ~0.7 and attach to the human's face, not the robot's side.

Background is specified as a split (bg/paper) but renders as one solid blue field — the brief calls for a visible blueprint-grid divide between the chaotic left and calm right; add the second panel color or a vertical grid line.
Top ~55% of the canvas is empty sky while every element is crammed into the bottom third; raise the ground line or scale up the building/robot/human group so the square is used more evenly.
The gift box under the robot reads as a vent grate/crate, not a present — add a bow or ribbon raw shape on top so 'stepping out of a gift-wrapped box' is legible.
Composition (blueprint building + falling chart + robot/human pair with labels above) is very close to at least two recent thumbnails; vary anchor heights or chart style for more novelty.

review.verdict: A clean, readable blueprint split-frame that gets the two-track joke across, but it narrowly passes: the robot's glasses hand-off doesn't visually connect (empty gesturing hand, glasses already on the human), and the whole split/divider/falling-chart/robot-with-box composition closely echoes the most recent slopper.
revisionNotes: Fix the glasses hand-off: attach the glasses prop to the robot's outstretched yellow hand (not the human's head) so it reads as an offer; right now the arm points at empty space and the human already appears to be wearing them.

Novelty: the split-frame divided by a vertical line, falling chart on the left, robot+gift-box+human cluster on right, closely repeats the most recent blueprint slopper's composition. Vary the divider device or swap the chart/box props.
Re-pose the robot's arm so the gesture resolves on a held object at the hand instead of floating toward the divider line with nothing in it — currently reads as a polish bug.
Per LESSONS.md, improvise the chair and gift box shapes a little differently from prior scenes using these same components to avoid visual repetition.
Consider giving the building's door a clearer open-swing (a visible door leaf at an angle) so 'door swinging open' reads instantly rather than as a static rectangle.
